IRS990.ActivityOrMissionDesc: ADVANCE CA LIFE SCIENCES ECOSYSTEM BY ADVOCATING PUBLIC POLICIES & SUPPORTING BUSINESSES.
IRS990.MissionDesc: CLSA ADVANCES CALIFORNIAS WORLD-LEADING LIFE SCIENCES INNOVATION ECOSYSTEM BY ADVOCATING FOR EFFECTIVE NATIONAL, STATE AND LOCAL PUBLIC POLICIES AND SUPPORTING ENTREPRENEURS AND LIFE SCIENCES BUSINESSES.
IRS990.Desc: PANTHEON AWARDS CEREMONY: EACH YEAR CLSA RECOGNIZES ACHIEVEMENT AND HONORS EXCELLENCE IN THE LIFE SCIENCES INDUSTRY IN CALIFORNIA, AS IT BRINGS TOGETHER HUNDREDS OF CALIFORNIAS LIFE SCIENCES INDUSTRY LEADERS. THE PANTHEON AWARDS CEREMONY IS A CELEBRATION OF THE CONTRIBUTIONS AND ACHIEVEMENTS OF THE STATE AND A MOMENT IN TIME TO PAUSE AND REFLECT ON THE INDUSTRYS LEGACY OVER THREE DECADES.

ProgSrvcAccomActy2Grp.Desc: Racial & Social Equity: The Racial & Social Equity Initiative is our bold plan to commit to change, a unified effort TO PROMOTE INCLUSIVE LEADERSHIP PRIMARILY THROUGH CAUCUS ENGAGEMENT AND WORKFORCE AND TALENT PROGRAMS.

ProgSrvcAccomActy3Grp.Desc: LIFE SCIENCES ACADEMY: LIFE SCIENCES ACADEMY IS DEDICATED TO EDUCATING POLICY MAKERSAND OPINION LEADERS ABOUT OUR INDUSTRY, INCREASING THEIR AWARENESS OF CALIFORNIASLIFE SCIENCES MOST PRESSING ISSUES IN SERVING PATIENTS AND IMPROVING THE QUALITY OFLIFE FOR RESIDENTS ACROSS CALIFORNIA.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Part I, Line 1a: Relevant information in regards to selections on 1a.
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: EMPLOYEES HAVE THE OPPORTUNITY TO JOIN A HEALTH CLUB FACILITY IN THEIR LOCAL AREA OR OTHERWISE PAY FOR HEALTH-RELATED ACTIVITIES. SUCH HEALTH-RELATED COSTS WILL BE COVERED FOR EMPLOYEES ONLY, WITH A MAXIMUM MONTHLY CHARGE OF $40.00.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Part I, Line 5b: Explanation of organization compensation based on revenues of related organization

SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: THE CALIFORNIA LIFE SCIENCES ASSOCIATION (CLSA) BOARD OF DIRECTORS EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE (THE COMMITTEE) FUNCTIONS AS THE COMPENSATION COMMITTEE FOR PURPOSES OF DETERMINING EXECUTIVE SALARY COMPARABILITY AND ENSURING ALL OF CLSAS COMPENSATION PRACTICES ARE CARRIED OUT IN A RESPONSIBLE MANNER AND ARE ALSO COMPLIANT WITH STATE AND FEDERAL REGULATIONS. THE COMMITTEE HAS OVERALL RESPONSIBILITY FOR EVALUATING THE PERFORMANCE AND COMPENSATION OF THE CEO AND CFO (EXECUTIVES). ANY CHANGES IN SALARY FOR THE EXECUTIVES WILL BE DETERMINED BY THE COMMITTEE, AND DOCUMENTATION IS KEPT OF ITS DELIBERATIONS REGARDING THE COMPENSATION OF THE EXECUTIVES. AFTER THE COMMITTEE HAS REVIEWED ITS FINDINGS REGARDING RELEVANT COMPARABILITY DATA, THE COMMITTEE WILL DECIDE UPON AN APPROPRIATE SALARY, BONUS, AND ANY OTHER FRINGE BENEFITS OR PERQUISITES. ANY SALARY CHANGES WILL BE EFFECTIVE ON AN AGREED UPON DATE.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Section B, Line 11b
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: A qualified and authorized person shall complete the annual form 990 information return under the direction of the President & CEO and CFO. The return shall be reviewed by the President & CEO and CFO for completeness and accuracy prior to its filing with the IRS. At the next board meeting, the chair of the finance committee or CFO may review the return with the board.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Section B, Line 12c
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: The CLSA Board of Directors and employees sign a questionnaire confirming compliance with the written conflict of interest policy and highlighting any potential conflicts. Additionally, CLSA has procedures in place to identify any potential conflicts of interest e.g., policies related to the review of all contracts and documentation supporting all cash disbursements by senior executives that are familiar with the need to identify such transactions (the CFO and/or President & CEO). Any potential or actual conflicts identified would be reviewed by the President & CEO and CFO with assistance from third-party attorneys and discussed with the Executive Committee of the Board of Directors to determine whether an actual or potential conflict of interest exists and, if it does, how it can be resolved. A summary of these activities would be reported to the Board of Directors at least annually.
